Дерево чистое (`git status` пуст). Волны 40–49 уже в дереве и уже проверены. Не проверяй их заново. Не читай AGENTS.md, docs/PLAN.md, docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, waves/ и sessions/ — для этой задачи они не нужны. Не запускай `./scripts/dev byte-compile-all` и `./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el` — это минуты ожидания, а провайдер в это время рвёт соединение. Проверяй только те два файла проверок, которые ты трогаешь.

Твоя работа — ровно два файла:
1. tests/checks/check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el — починить.
2. spec.json — зарегистрировать два claim'а.

ДЕФЕКТ, КОТОРЫЙ ТЫ ЧИНИШЬ (файл 1). Сейчас эта проверка падает:
    bridge-race: the claim of the bridge declares no control to run
и возвращает код 1. Проверка берёт control claim'а `bridge-keeps-the-answer` из spec.json функцией `yeah-check--control-of` и не находит его, хотя control в spec.json есть. Причина в том, как Emacs 30.2 отдаёт ключи объекта, прочитанного json-read-file: они могут прийти символами, а не строками. Проверь это и исправь чтение spec.json так, чтобы control находился; больше в этой проверке ничего не меняй.

После правки `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el` обязан вернуть 0 на целом мосте. Эта проверка сама делает десять прогонов проверки моста против control'а claim'а `bridge-keeps-the-answer` и требует, чтобы каждый прогон упал на своём утверждении "bridge-keep:" (код 1), а не на краше и не на таймауте.

ЧТО ЗАРЕГИСТРИРОВАТЬ В spec.json (файл 2):
- Claim `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — оставь как есть, если его control кусается десять раз из десяти. Если нет — замени control на такой, который кусается всегда.
- Новый claim `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction`:
    "text": "the check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the control, and the control bites on each of them"
    "scope": ["lib/yeah-bridge.el", "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el", "tests/checks/check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el"]
    "requirements": [{"kind": "verifier", "spec": "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el"}]
    "falsifier": "the check of the bridge gives different verdicts on consecutive runs of the control, or the control does not bite on each of them"
    "register": "fact"
    "control": одна shell-команда (sed), которая ломает детерминизм проверки: если убрать удержание ответа в tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el, проверка перестаёт распоряжаться предметом, control claim'а моста перестаёт кусаться, и проверка волны обязана упасть на своём же утверждении.
  Остальные поля (source, kind, phase, owner, review_on, waiver) — как у соседних claim'ов.

Правила правки spec.json: это JSON; массивы в нём записаны в одну строку; вставляй текстом, а не перегенерируй файл скриптом; кавычки внутри строк экранируются как \". После правки проверь: python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('spec.json'));print('ok')".

КРИТЕРИИ ВЫХОДА:
1. Проверка волны проходит без control'а (код 0).
2. Десять последовательных прогонов control'а claim'а `bridge-keeps-the-answer` кусаются, каждый падает на утверждении проверки.
3. Control нового claim'а ломает детерминизм: после его применения проверка волны падает на своём утверждении.

Каждый твой ответ — это вызов инструмента, а не описание следующего шага. Начни с правки файла 1. Когда работа сделана и проверена, вызови инструмент finish и вкратце скажи, что изменилось и чем ты это проверил.

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el --- the check of the bridge decides the race by construction -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The check of the bridge used to race the subject: it kept a thread
;; spinning to make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached
;; Emacs a hundred and twenty times, and failed only when the answer
;; was really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim of the bridge came out `inconclusive' and the map came
;; out `unknown'.  An evidence that decides its verdict by a race
;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A
;; run that crashes Emacs, a run that hangs and a run that passes are
;; all failures of this check.
;;
;; The check of the bridge must also pass on the whole bridge, before
;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

;;; Code:

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (or (locate-dominating-file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)
                              "spec.json")
      default-directory)
  "The root of the repository: the directory that holds `spec.json'.
The check knows where it is by the specification it reads, and not by
the depth of its own file.")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  "How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  "Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el"
  "The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.")

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  "Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it."
  (let* ((json-object-type 'alist)
         (spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name "spec.json" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (alist-get "claims" spec))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (alist-get "id" entry) claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (alist-get "control" claim))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  "Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET."
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  "Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY."
  (list yeah-check--emacs "-Q" "--batch"
        "-L" (expand-file-name "lib" directory)
        "-L" directory
        "-l" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let ((output "")
        (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  "Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.
Return the list of the failures of the check."
  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of "bridge-keeps-the-answer"))
        (directory (make-temp-file "yeah-bridge-control-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push "the claim of the bridge declares no control to run" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "lib" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "lib" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "tests" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "tests" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format "the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format "the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p "bridge-keep:" words))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "bridge-race: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el ends here

;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A

;; all failures of this check.

;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (or (locate-dominating-file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)
                              "spec.json")
      default-directory)
  "The root of the repository: the directory that holds `spec.json'.
The check knows where it is by the specification it reads, and not by
the depth of its own file.")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  "How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  "Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el"
  "The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.")

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  "Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it."
  (let* ((json-object-type 'alist)
         (spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name "spec.json" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (alist-get "claims" spec))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (alist-get "id" entry) claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (alist-get "control" claim))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  "Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET."
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  "Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY."
  (list yeah-check--emacs "-Q" "--batch"
        "-L" (expand-file-name "lib" directory)
        "-L" directory
        "-l" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.

run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let ((output "")
        (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))

        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))

                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))

              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  "Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.

  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of "bridge-keeps-the-answer"))
        (directory (make-temp-file "yeah-bridge-control-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push "the claim of the bridge declares no control to run" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "lib" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "lib" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "tests" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "tests" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format "the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format "the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p "bridge-keep:" words))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "bridge-race: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el --- the check of the bridge decides the race by construction -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The check of the bridge used to race the subject: it kept a thread
;; spinning to make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached
;; Emacs a hundred and twenty times, and failed only when the answer
;; was really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim of the bridge came out `inconclusive' and the map came
;; out `unknown'.  An evidence that decides its verdict by a race
;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A
;; run that crashes Emacs, a run that hangs and a run that passes are
;; all failures of this check.
;;
;; The check of the bridge must also pass on the whole bridge, before
;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

;;; Code:

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (or (locate-dominating-file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)
                              "spec.json")
      default-directory)
  "The root of the repository: the directory that holds `spec.json'.
The check knows where it is by the specification it reads, and not by
the depth of its own file.")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  "How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  "Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el"
  "The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.")

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  "Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it."
  (let* ((json-object-type 'alist)
         (spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name "spec.json" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (alist-get "claims" spec))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (alist-get "id" entry) claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (alist-get "control" claim))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  "Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET."
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  "Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY."
  (list yeah-check--emacs "-Q" "--batch"
        "-L" (expand-file-name "lib" directory)
        "-L" directory
        "-l" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let ((output "")
        (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  "Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.
Return the list of the failures of the check."
  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of "bridge-keeps-the-answer"))
        (directory (make-temp-file "yeah-bridge-control-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push "the claim of the bridge declares no control to run" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "lib" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "lib" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "tests" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "tests" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format "the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format "the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p "bridge-keep:" words))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "bridge-race: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el ends here

# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defconst yeah-check--answer "live text"
  "The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  "Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  "The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  "The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  "The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  "Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none."
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  "Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value."
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  "Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone."
  (let ((filter (yeah-check--filter-of args)))
    (if (and filter yeah-check--hold-the-answer)
        (progn
          (setq yeah-check--held-filter filter)
          (let ((process
                 (apply orig-fun
                        (append (yeah-check--without-filter args)
                                (list :filter
                                      (lambda (_process chunk)
                                        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk
                                              (concat yeah-check--held-chunk
                                                      chunk))))))))
            (setq yeah-check--held-process process)
            process))
      (apply orig-fun args))))

(defun yeah-check--around-accept-process-output (orig-fun &optional process &rest args)
  "Run the event loop of Emacs, and give the held answer to the bridge.
The answer of the child is delivered when the bridge asks for the
pending output of a process that is gone: the bridge reads the answer
of the child after its exit, which is the condition the defect is
about."
  (let ((result (apply orig-fun process (or args (list 0.05)))))
    (when (and yeah-check--hold-the-answer
               (null process)
               yeah-check--held-chunk
               yeah-check--held-filter)

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-

;;; Commentary:

;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defconst yeah-check--answer "live text"
  "The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  "Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  "The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  "The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  "The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  "Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none."
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  "Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value."
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  "Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone."

        (progn

                        (append (yeah-check--without-filter args)
                                (list :filter
                                      (lambda (_process chunk)
                                        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk
                                              (concat yeah-check--held-chunk
                                                      chunk))))))))
            (setq yeah-check--held-process process)
            process))
      (apply orig-fun args))))

(defun yeah-check--around-accept-process-output (orig-fun &optional process &rest args)
  "Run the event loop of Emacs, and give the held answer to the bridge.
The answer of the child is delivered when the bridge asks for the
pending output of a process that is gone: the bridge reads the answer
of the child after its exit, which is the condition the defect is
about."

               (null process)

               yeah-check--held-filter)

        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk nil)
        (funcall yeah-check--held-filter yeah-check--held-process chunk)))
    result))

(defun yeah-check--advise (symbol function)
  "Advise SYMBOL with FUNCTION.
Emacs 30 asks for the kind of the advice and the older Emacs does
not; the advice itself takes the original function as its first
argument in both."
  (if (>= emacs-major-version 30)
      (advice-add symbol :around function)
    (advice-add symbol function)))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000))))

      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"

        (yeah-check--advise 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
        (yeah-check--advise 'accept-process-output
                            #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)
        (unwind-protect
            (let ((text (condition-case err
                           (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                                 (yeah-bridge-server name))
                             (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                         (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
              (unless (equal yeah-check--answer text)
                (push (format "the bridge lost the answer: it answered %S" text)
                      failures)))
          (advice-remove 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
          (advice-remove 'accept-process-output
                         #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)))

    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)")))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defconst yeah-check--answer "live text"
  "The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  "Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  "The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  "The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  "The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  "Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none."
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  "Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value."
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  "Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone."
  (let ((filter (yeah-check--filter-of args)))
    (if (and filter yeah-check--hold-the-answer)
        (progn
          (setq yeah-check--held-filter filter)
          (let ((process
                 (apply orig-fun
                        (append (yeah-check--without-filter args)
                                (list :filter
                                      (lambda (_process chunk)
                                        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk
                                              (concat yeah-check--held-chunk
                                                      chunk))))))))
            (setq yeah-check--held-process process)
            process))
      (apply orig-fun args))))

(defun yeah-check--around-accept-process-output (orig-fun &optional process &rest args)
  "Run the event loop of Emacs, and give the held answer to the bridge.
The answer of the child is delivered when the bridge asks for the
pending output of a process that is gone: the bridge reads the answer
of the child after its exit, which is the condition the defect is
about."
  (let ((result (apply orig-fun process (or args (list 0.05)))))
    (when (and yeah-check--hold-the-answer
               (null process)
               yeah-check--held-chunk
               yeah-check--held-filter)
      (let ((chunk yeah-check--held-chunk))
        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk nil)
        (funcall yeah-check--held-filter yeah-check--held-process chunk)))
    result))

(defun yeah-check--advise (symbol function)
  "Advise SYMBOL with FUNCTION.
Emacs 30 asks for the kind of the advice and the older Emacs does
not; the advice itself takes the original function as its first
argument in both."
  (if (>= emacs-major-version 30)
      (advice-add symbol :around function)
    (advice-add symbol function)))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000))))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        (format (concat "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") "
                                        "(insert \"%s\"))")
                                yeah-check--answer))
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; the hooks of the check: the answer of the child waits for the
        ;; bridge to ask for the pending output of a process that is gone
        (yeah-check--advise 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
        (yeah-check--advise 'accept-process-output
                            #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)
        (unwind-protect
            (let ((text (condition-case err
                           (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                                 (yeah-bridge-server name))
                             (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                         (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
              (unless (equal yeah-check--answer text)
                (push (format "the bridge lost the answer: it answered %S" text)
                      failures)))
          (advice-remove 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
          (advice-remove 'accept-process-output
                         #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)))
    ;; stop the server
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)")))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

;;; yeah-bridge.el --- the emacsclient bridge -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
;; it under the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; An explicit, permissioned bridge to the buffers of an attached
;; Emacs, reached through `emacsclient'.  The bridge is a capability
;; and not a convenience: the two tools carry their own names, so
;; the permission system can approve `bridge__eval' and
;; `bridge__buffer_read' separately, and nothing enters the tool
;; registry until the operator asks for it with `yeah-bridge-register'.
;;
;; The program is started with `make-process' -- never through a
;; shell -- and every call is bounded by a short timeout, so a busy
;; or absent server cannot hang the agent.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-tools)

(defgroup yeah-bridge nil
  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-program "emacsclient"
  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.
The program is run directly, without a shell, so it must be an
executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-server nil
  "Name of the Emacs server the bridge connects to.
When nil, `emacsclient' connects to the default server.  A service
placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."
  :type '(choice (const nil) string)
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defconst yeah-bridge--timeout 2
  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

(defconst yeah-bridge--probe "t"
  "Expression evaluated to find out whether the attached Emacs answers.")

(defun yeah-bridge--program-path ()
  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.
The program is not found when `yeah-bridge-program' is empty or
names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

(defun yeah-bridge--trim (text)
  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

(defun yeah-bridge--stderr-text (buffer)
  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer
    (buffer-string)))

(defun yeah-bridge--wait (process timeout)
  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.
Return non-nil when the process exited in time."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))
    (while (and (process-live-p process)
                (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output process 0.05))
    (not (process-live-p process))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run-program (path args timeout)
  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.
Return a plist with the keys `:ok', `:status', `:output' and
`:message'; see `yeah-bridge--run' for their meaning."
  (let ((output "")
        (stderr-buffer (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge stderr*"))
        (process nil))
    (unwind-protect
        (condition-case err
            (progn
              (setq process (make-process
                             :name "yeah-bridge"
                             :command (cons path args)
                             :connection-type 'pipe
                             :noquery t
                             :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                             :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                                       (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                             :stderr stderr-buffer))
              (yeah-bridge--wait process timeout)
              (let ((timed-out (process-live-p process)))
                (when timed-out
                  (ignore-errors (kill-process process)))
                ;; A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
                ;; filter: the answer of the attached Emacs is then lost
                ;; and the bridge answers with nothing.  Draining the
                ;; pending events after the exit — until the output stops
                ;; changing — gives the filter its last words.
                (let ((previous nil)
                      (drain-deadline (+ (float-time) 0.2)))
                  (while (and (< (float-time) drain-deadline)
                              (not (equal previous output)))
                    (setq previous output)
                    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
                (let ((status (unless timed-out (process-exit-status process))))
                  (list :ok (and (not timed-out) (eq status 0))
                        :status status
                        :output (yeah-bridge--trim output)
                        :message
                        (cond
                         (timed-out
                          (format "the attached Emacs did not answer within %s seconds"
                                  timeout))
                         ((not (eq status 0))
                          (let ((text (yeah-bridge--trim
                                       (yeah-bridge--stderr-text stderr-buffer))))
                            (if (> (length text) 0)
                                (format "the attached Emacs reported: %s" text)
                              "the attached Emacs reported an error")))
                         (t nil))))))
          (error
           (list :ok nil
                 :status nil
                 :output ""
                 :message (error-message-string err))))
      (when (and process (process-live-p process))
        (ignore-errors (delete-process process)))
      (when (buffer-live-p stderr-buffer)
        (kill-buffer stderr-buffer)))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run (args &optional timeout)
  "Run the bridge program with ARGS and collect what it printed.
ARGS is the list of command-line arguments without the program
itself.  TIMEOUT is the number of seconds the process may run.

Return a plist with the keys `:ok' (non-nil when the program
answered successfully), `:status' (the exit status), `:output' (the
standard output without trailing newlines) and `:message' (why the
call failed, or nil)."
  (let ((path (yeah-bridge--program-path))
        (args (append (when (and (stringp yeah-bridge-server)
                                 (> (length yeah-bridge-server) 0))
                        (list "-s" yeah-bridge-server))
                      args)))
    (if (null path)
        (list :ok nil
              :status nil
              :output ""
              :message (format "the bridge program %S is not executable"
                               yeah-bridge-program))
      (yeah-bridge--run-program path args (or timeout yeah-bridge--timeout)))))

(defun yeah-bridge-available-p ()
  "Return non-nil when the attached Emacs answers the bridge program.
The program must be executable and the attached Emacs must reply
within the bridge timeout.  This never signals: any failure means
that the bridge is unavailable."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" yeah-bridge--probe))))
        (and (plist-get result :ok)
             (> (length (or (plist-get result :output) "")) 0)))
    (error nil)))

(defun yeah-bridge-eval (expression)
  "Evaluate EXPRESSION in the attached Emacs and return the printed result.
EXPRESSION is a string of Elisp code.  The result is the printed
value, as a string, without trailing newlines.

Signals `user-error' when the bridge is unavailable and when the
evaluation itself fails; the message says which of the two happened."
  (unless (stringp expression)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-bridge-eval: expression must be a string, got %S"
                          (type-of expression)))))
  (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" expression))))
    (if (plist-get result :ok)
        (plist-get result :output)
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-bridge-eval: %s"
                            (if (yeah-bridge-available-p)
                                (format "evaluation failed: %s"
                                        (or (plist-get result :message)
                                            "unknown error"))
                              "the bridge is unavailable")))))))

(defun yeah-bridge--decode (output)
  "Return the string OUTPUT holds, decoding its printed form.
`emacsclient --eval' prints the value of the evaluation: a string
arrives quoted, as its printed form.  When OUTPUT looks like a printed
string it is read back; anything else is returned unchanged."
  (if (and (stringp output)
           (> (length output) 1)
           (eq (aref output 0) ?\"))
      (condition-case nil (read output) (error output))
    output))

(defun yeah-bridge-buffer-read (name)
  "Return the text of the live buffer NAME of the attached Emacs.
NAME is the name of a buffer in the attached Emacs.  The result is
its text, as a string, without trailing newlines.

Signals `user-error' when the bridge is unavailable and when the
buffer cannot be read there; the message says which of the two
happened."

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el --- the check of the bridge decides the race by construction -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The check of the bridge used to race the subject: it kept a thread
;; spinning to make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached
;; Emacs a hundred and twenty times, and failed only when the answer
;; was really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim of the bridge came out `inconclusive' and the map came
;; out `unknown'.  An evidence that decides its verdict by a race
;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A
;; run that crashes Emacs, a run that hangs and a run that passes are
;; all failures of this check.
;;
;; The check of the bridge must also pass on the whole bridge, before
;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

;;; Code:

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (or (locate-dominating-file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)
                              "spec.json")
      default-directory)
  "The root of the repository: the directory that holds `spec.json'.
The check knows where it is by the specification it reads, and not by
the depth of its own file.")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  "How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  "Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el"
  "The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.")

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  "Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it."
  (let* ((json-object-type 'alist)
         (spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name "spec.json" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (alist-get "claims" spec))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (alist-get "id" entry) claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (alist-get "control" claim))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  "Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET."
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  "Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY."
  (list yeah-check--emacs "-Q" "--batch"
        "-L" (expand-file-name "lib" directory)
        "-L" directory
        "-l" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let ((output "")
        (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  "Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.
Return the list of the failures of the check."
  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of "bridge-keeps-the-answer"))
        (directory (make-temp-file "yeah-bridge-control-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push "the claim of the bridge declares no control to run" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "lib" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "lib" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "tests" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "tests" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format "the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format "the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p "bridge-keep:" words))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "bridge-race: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el ends here

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let* ((output "")
         (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
         (process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))
